text:
A: Hiya! Oh, finally, it's you! I've been hoping I'd get you. Can you hear me alright?
B: Yes! Hello! I was hoping also, honestly. I saw your photo at the beginning and I thought, she looks so friendly.
A: Oh, stop it, you'll set me off! I'm Joanne, Taunton.
B: Agnieszka, Basingstoke. Lee said you were nice, actually. He told me about his drop links.
A: Ha! Did he fix your car over the video? He's a good lad, that one, bit grumpy about his boss, mind.
B: He diagnosed it in thirty seconds. I wrote it down for my husband.
A: Oh, that's brilliant. So what do you do, then? I'm guessing something organised, with that calendar behind you.
B: Executive assistant, for a CFO at insurance company. Diary, board papers, travel, all of it. I check everything three times, sorry, four times sometimes.
A: Oh, I'd be the same. I used to do the rota at the practice, I was head vet nurse before my back went, and I'd lie awake thinking, have I put two people on the Saturday? Erm, I'm not working now, three years, I just help at a cat rescue. And I keep thinking about a little part-time job, reception or something, but then I think, oh, they won't want me, I'm out of the loop. Sorry, I've said that to about four people today!
B: But you should go for it! You know animals, you know people. And reception, honestly, it's mostly being calm when someone is panicking. That's half my job too.
A: That's what Shahida said! Well, sort of, she was a bit sterner about it.
B: Ha, yes, she's very direct. I liked her.
A: Oh, me too, in the end. Have you got children?
B: One, Zosia, she's nine. Swimming Thursdays, Polish school Saturdays.
A: Oh, busy girl. Mine are grown up now, twenty-two and nineteen. Ellie's at uni in Cardiff and I worry about her constantly, living in a city, walking home at night, all that. She rings when she wants money and I'm just relieved she's alive!
B: I think I will be the same. Already I worry and she's only nine.
A: Oh, it doesn't stop, love. Do you do anything for yourself?
B: Pilates, Tuesday evenings, with a friend from work. And walking at lunchtime.
A: No! I do Pilates on a Tuesday! Mornings, though. I'm always shattered after.
B: Me too, and it's only stretching, how is it so tiring?
A: I know! And musicals? You look like a musicals person.
B: Oh yes. Les Misérables, twice in London. I cried both times, the whole second half.
A: Oh, "Bring Him Home", I'm gone every time. We're doing ABBA at choir, not quite the same.
B: ABBA is happy crying, at least.
A: That's true! Oh, and my hanging baskets haven't taken this year, would you believe.
B: Mine died in the heatwave! Everybody's baskets are dead today, I think.
A: It's a national tragedy. Oh, we must be nearly out of time.
B: I think so. It was so nice to talk, really.
